Phase 1 first. A full run takes about 40 minutes, so a loop at full size can never meet the
"seconds, not minutes" gate, and small inputs come out right, so a tiny fixture will not go
red either. That is the slow-loop path:

1. Shrink the input until it still goes red. Halve the cells, seeded and by sample, and rerun
   until the loss disappears; keep the smallest size that still drops cells.
2. Restart from the last good intermediate file. The cells are all present in the table that
   goes into the merge step, so save that table once and start each run at the merge, which
   skips the steps before it.
3. If a run still takes minutes, accept a batch job as the loop: one command that runs the
   merge on the saved input and asserts that the cell count going in equals the count coming
   out, run unattended, with each run cut to the minimum.

Its red signal is your symptom, cells lost across the merge, so it can go green once fixed.
